title: CT4 Example 2

questions.prompt: A Kubernetes namespace alone guarantees network isolation and a separate host kernel.
questions.explanation: A namespace is not, by itself, either of those isolation boundaries.

questions.prompt: Client-side validation can replace server-side validation because all users must use the supplied interface.
questions.explanation: Requests can bypass the client; the server must enforce its own constraints.

questions.prompt: Parameterised queries separate bound values from query syntax, but they do not decide whether the caller may access the returned rows.
questions.explanation: Injection prevention and object authorisation are separate responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Match each concept to the description that best distinguishes it.
options: Exercises a running application to observe externally visible behaviour
Examines dependencies and associated component risks
Provides an inventory of software components
Examines source or a related code representation without running the application

items.answer: Examines source or a related code representation without running the application
items.explanation: SAST: Examines source or a related code representation without running the application.

items.answer: Exercises a running application to observe externally visible behaviour
items.explanation: DAST: Exercises a running application to observe externally visible behaviour.

items.answer: Examines dependencies and associated component risks
items.explanation: SCA: Examines dependencies and associated component risks.

items.answer: Provides an inventory of software components
items.explanation: SBOM: Provides an inventory of software components.

questions.prompt: A latent fault must cause an observed failure every time the program runs.
questions.explanation: Specific inputs, states or conditions may be required to activate a defect.

questions.prompt: L4 connection balancing necessarily distributes each stream inside one long-lived HTTP/2 connection to a different backend.
questions.explanation: Multiplexed streams may remain pinned to the backend selected for that connection.

questions.prompt: Complete the statement using the word bank. Use each term at most once: fault; failure; operating; repair; formatting; encryption. “A static defect is a [1]; observed incorrect runtime behaviour is a [2]. MTTF measures mean [3] time until failure, whereas MTTR measures mean [4] time.”

items.explanation: A fault is a static defect.
A failure is observed erroneous runtime behaviour.
Use the stated measurement scope for mean operating time.
MTTR concerns repair/restoration under the chosen convention.

questions.prompt: A good performance report may omit errors if its p95 latency is below the required threshold.
questions.explanation: Every mandatory acceptance criterion matters, and fast failures can distort latency summaries.

questions.prompt: Using AI assistance while inspecting and verifying the generated implementation is different from the narrow “vibe coding” workflow used in the guide.
questions.explanation: The narrower definition concerns largely accepting generated behaviour without inspecting its code; the tool alone does not determine the workflow.

questions.prompt: Which of the following practices support a defensible technical presentation? Select all that apply.
options: Connect a design mechanism to its requirement and trade-off.
Describe planned features as already tested to keep the story simple.
Report observations with their tested conditions and limitations.
Rehearse a meaningful demo and clearly identify fallback material.
Use a framework’s popularity as proof of system quality.
questions.explanation: Rationale, bounded evidence and rehearsed honest demonstrations help an audience assess the work. Popularity and misrepresented status do not.

questions.prompt: Exporting all application records proves that proprietary workflow logic and permissions can be migrated without additional work.
questions.explanation: Record export and portability of runnable behaviour are distinct concerns.

questions.prompt: Match each test situation to the most specific testing purpose.

items.prompt: Existing response-time checks are rerun after a feature change
items.explanation: Existing response-time checks are rerun after a feature change: Non-functional regression testing.

items.prompt: Storage and queries are evaluated with a much larger dataset
items.explanation: Storage and queries are evaluated with a much larger dataset: Volume testing.

items.prompt: Real API and database components exchange data in a test environment
items.explanation: Real API and database components exchange data in a test environment: Integration testing.

items.prompt: Selected users complete tasks while obstacles are observed
items.explanation: Selected users complete tasks while obstacles are observed: Usability testing.

questions.prompt: Match the measure to the property it reports.
options: A distribution position rather than the maximum latency

items.explanation: Throughput: Completed work per unit time.

items.answer: A distribution position rather than the maximum latency
items.explanation: p95 latency: A distribution position rather than the maximum latency.

questions.prompt: Relate each symptom to the most relevant corrective practice.
options: Automate shared checks and review actual compliance
Use operation identity, idempotency and reconciliation
Establish durable ownership and managed credentials
Revoke or rotate exposed credentials and investigate use

items.prompt: Secrets remain valid after being deleted from the latest commit
items.answer: Revoke or rotate exposed credentials and investigate use
items.explanation: Secrets remain valid after being deleted from the latest commit: Revoke or rotate exposed credentials and investigate use.

items.prompt: Style rules exist only in a document
items.answer: Automate shared checks and review actual compliance
items.explanation: Style rules exist only in a document: Automate shared checks and review actual compliance.

items.prompt: A generated workflow repeats a reservation after a timeout
items.answer: Use operation identity, idempotency and reconciliation
items.explanation: A generated workflow repeats a reservation after a timeout: Use operation identity, idempotency and reconciliation.

items.prompt: A critical application depends on one person’s account
items.answer: Establish durable ownership and managed credentials
items.explanation: A critical application depends on one person’s account: Establish durable ownership and managed credentials.

notes: Original practice paper based on the reference assessment style. Not an official paper or prediction. No official duration was available in the supplied export.
multiRule: Each correct selection earns the question marks divided by the number of correct options. Each incorrect selection deducts the same amount. Omitted options earn zero. Each question is floored at zero. This explicit practice rule is not asserted to be the original marking formula.
